title: Manager, SOX PMO - Business Process
description: GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster. The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software. * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. An overview of this role As Manager, SOX PMO - Business Process, you'll lead Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) compliance for assigned business processes as part of GitLab's second line. This is advisory work, not repeatable testing: you'll deeply understand how processes work, evaluate risks as the business changes, and help control owners design and remediate controls that hold up to audit. Judgment matters more than procedure. You'll form well-supported conclusions, align with control owners and Internal Audit, and defend positions to external auditors. GitLab already uses AI extensively, and the next phase brings AI agents into our SOX processes. You'll help teams adopt them with confidence, finding creative ways to enable new ways of working while maintaining compliance. You'll also partner with the information technology (IT) SOX PMO on readiness for new systems and applications. This role reports to the Senior Director, SOX PMO, within the Chief Accounting Officer's organization. What You’ll Do    Lead SOX compliance for assigned business processes as the second-line subject matter expert, advising control owners who own and operate the controls. Deeply understand each process, its systems and data flows, and resolve open questions and assumptions early. Monitor risks from new and changing processes, products, and systems. Help control owners design, strengthen, or right-size controls, and contribute to the annual SOX risk assessment and scoping. Evaluate control deficiencies individually and in aggregate, identify root causes, and prepare well-supported severity assessments. Work with management to develop, implement, and monitor remediation plans. Prepare auditor-ready technical memos on sampling methodology, scoping, and control rationalization, using independent analysis and sound conclusions. Prepare reports and presentations on SOX compliance status for leadership. Lead business walkthroughs and stakeholder meetings, and coordinate with Internal Audit and external auditors throughout the audit. Anticipate questions, support positions with data and judgment, and escalate risks and auditor comments promptly with a recommended path forward. Advise on controls for AI-enabled processes and processes that use AI agents. Find opportunities to automate SOX work using AI tools, and validate their output. Partner with the IT SOX PMO to assess new systems and controls, including application controls and key reports. Develop and maintain accurate process narratives, flowcharts, and risk and control matrices as processes change. Collaborate with Finance, Operations, Legal, Human Resources, Sales, Engineering, and IT leaders to help them design and maintain effective business controls. What You’ll Bring  Hands-on SOX and internal controls experience in control design, remediation, and deficiency evaluation, beyond testing alone. Experience in the software or technology industry is required; SOX PMO, Big Four risk advisory, or assurance experience is a strong plus. A bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; an active Certified Public Accountant (CPA) credential (strongly preferred) or Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) credential. A strong understanding of SOX requirements and internal control frameworks, such as the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO) framework. Professional judgment and skepticism: verifying facts against source documents, testing the reasonableness of data and conclusions, and recognizing missing information. title: Project Manager, PCI DSS Compliance
description: Calling all innovators – find your future at Fiserv. We’re Fiserv, a global leader in Fintech and payments, and we move money and information in a way that moves the world. We connect financial institutions, corporations, merchants, and consumers to one another millions of times a day – quickly, reliably, and securely. Any time you swipe your credit card, pay through a mobile app, or withdraw money from the bank, we’re involved. If you want to make an impact on a global scale, come make a difference at Fiserv. Job Title Project Manager, PCI DSS Compliance What does a successful Project Manager, PCI DSS Compliance do at Fiserv? The Project Manager, PCI DSS Compliance leads Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) initiatives across Commercial Middle Market, covering readiness, assessment support, governance, evidence collection, and control remediation. Partnering closely with compliance, security, technology, product, legal, operations, sales, implementation, and client-facing teams, this role translates regulatory requirements into executable work plans, clear deliverables, and sustainable operating practices while keeping risks, dependencies, and stakeholder commitments visible. As capacity permits, the role also manages prioritized Commercial Middle Market Operations projects to improve controls, processes, reporting, and execution. What you will do: Lead end-to-end project management for Commercial Middle Market initiatives involving PCI DSS compliance, readiness, assessments, remediation, and ongoing control sustainability. Apply strong working knowledge of PCI DSS requirements, testing expectations, evidence needs, control ownership, scoping considerations, and remediation practices to guide project planning and execution. Translate PCI DSS requirements and identified gaps into project charters, work breakdown structures, milestones, accountable owners, dependencies, risks, and measurable completion criteria. Coordinate readiness reviews, evidence collection, documentation, stakeholder responses, remediation plans, and validation activities in support of internal reviews and external assessments. Maintain clear governance through status reports, RAID logs, decision logs, action trackers, control-owner matrices, compliance calendars, and executive-ready milestone reporting. Facilitate cross-functional working sessions to confirm scope, interpret project impacts, resolve ownership gaps, track evidence and remediation, and drive timely decisions. Identify and escalate compliance risks, overdue actions, control deficiencies, and delivery blockers with clear business impact, options, and recommended actions. Partner with control owners to embed sustainable procedures, documentation, monitoring, and recurring governance that support continued PCI DSS compliance after project completion. Communicate PCI DSS project status, risks, dependencies, and required decisions clearly to senior leaders, technical teams, business partners, and other stakeholders. Secondarily, manage prioritized Commercial Middle Market Operations projects involving process improvement, reporting, implementation handoffs, governance, controls, and cross-functional execution. What you need to have: 6+ years of project or program management experience, including direct responsibility for information security, compliance, risk, audit, payments, or similarly regulated initiatives. High-level knowledge of PCI DSS, including requirements, scoping concepts, evidence expectations, control ownership, assessment readiness, remediation, and ongoing compliance obligations. Demonstrated experience managing complex, cross-functional compliance or technology projects with multiple stakeholders, dependencies, timelines, risks, and deliverables. Ability to translate technical and compliance requirements into clear business actions, accountable work plans, executive reporting, and sustainable operating processes. Strong experience creating project plans, RAID logs, remediation trackers, evidence inventories, governance materials, meeting recaps, and stakeholder communications. Proven ability to communicate compliance status, risks, findings, and recommendations clearly to senior leaders and technical and non-technical teams. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience. What would be nice to have: Experience leading PCI DSS readiness, assessment, remediation, or compliance-sustainment initiatives within merchant services, payment processing, financial services, or fintech. PCI Professional, Internal Security Assessor, PCIP, or other relevant PCI Security Standards Council credential. PMP, Agile/Scrum, Lean Six Sigma, Prosci, or comparable project or change-management certification. Experience partnering with information security, technology, compliance, risk, audit, legal, product, and operations teams.
